content.text: All three reports read cleanly. Before computing, I checked whether each month's stated cost total matches its line items — June's doesn't (a discrepancy worth flagging). Let me compute and write the file with a script for exact rounding:

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json

rev = {"may": 412380, "jun": 431205, "jul": 389640}
# stated totals per report
costs = {"may": 151120, "jun": 158240, "jul": 158280}
# line-item sums
lines = {
    "may": [96400, 21310, 18650, 9240, 5520],
    "jun": [98100, 23940, 21400, 10180, 4920],
    "jul": [98100, 24760, 16980, 12310, 6130],
}
for m in costs:
    s = sum(lines[m])
    print(m, "stated", costs[m], "line-sum", s, "diff", s - costs[m])

q_rev = sum(rev.values()); q_cost = sum(costs.values()); q_net = q_rev - q_cost
margin = round(q_net / q_rev * 100, 1)
adds = (86-17) + (74-22) + (63-31)
opened = 342+361+298; closed = 315+350+291
close_rate = round(closed / opened * 100, 1)
jun_g = round((rev["jun"] - rev["may"]) / rev["may"] * 100, 1)
jul_g = round((rev["jul"] - rev["jun"]) / rev["jun"] * 100, 1)

out = {
  "q_revenue_eur": q_rev,
  "q_costs_eur": q_cost,
  "q_net_eur": q_net,
  "margin_pct": margin,
  "net_customer_adds": adds,
  "ticket_close_rate_pct": close_rate,
  "june_revenue_growth_pct": jun_g,
  "july_revenue_growth_pct": jul_g,
  "notes": ("June cost line items sum to EUR 158,540 but the report states a total of EUR 158,240 "
            "(EUR 300 discrepancy; stated total used). July revenue fell 9.6% vs June, churn rose "
            "month over month (17 -> 22 -> 31), and new signups declined (86 -> 74 -> 63).")
}
with open("RESULTS.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    f.write("\n")
print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
EOF
